accessibility:
- The root `Menu` renders as `<aside class="menu">`. A menu that's navigation is better inside a
  `<nav>` with an `aria-label`, which gives assistive tech a navigation landmark to jump to.
- Every `Menu.List` has `role="list"`, nested ones included. That's the role a `<ul>` already has,
  set again for Safari, whose WebKit stops exposing a `<ul>` as a list once its markers are hidden,
  as Bulma's reset hides them, unless the role is written out.
- `Menu.Item active` sets `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, the link by
  default, so the current item isn't only a color. An `aria-current` you pass wins: a menu of
  sections on one page can say `"location"`, and `aria-current={false}` turns it off.
- Use semantic nesting (`Menu.List` inside `Menu.Item`) for submenus.
- Give each item an `href`, a router link through `as`, or `as="button"`, so the keyboard can
  reach it.
- `Menu.Item as="button"` defaults to `type="button"`, so a menu item inside a form doesn't
  submit it. Pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"` and yours is used instead; any other value
  renders `type="button"`.
- In forced colors (Windows' contrast themes), the browser replaces Bulma's fill and text color
  for the active item along with every other color, so bestax's stylesheet marks an
  `is-active` or `is-selected` item with a bar in the system's highlight color along its start
  edge there instead. The item's text, and an icon or a tag inside it, keep the colors your
  contrast theme gives them. That rule ships in `bestax.css` and `extras.css`, not in Bulma's
  own stylesheet.

:::note
For router integrations, pass the correct `as` and `to`/`href` props to `Menu.Item`.
:::

parts.summary: MenuList applies `menu-list` class only at the top level (not for nested lists). Every level renders `role="list"`, which Safari needs: WebKit stops exposing a `<ul>` as a list once its markers are hidden, and Bulma's reset hides them.

extraProps.name: role
extraProps.description: Ignored: every level renders `role="list"` in its place, so a menu or tree role can't go here.

parts.catchAll: All standard <ul> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: MenuItem supports `as` prop for custom link components, e.g., react-router-dom Link. Give each item an `href`, a router link through `as`, or `as="button"`, so the keyboard can reach it: an `<a>` with no `href` isn't a link, and Tab skips it.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component (e.g. `Link` from router). `'button'` renders `type="button"` unless you pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"`, so an item inside a form does not submit it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the wrapping `<li>`.

props.name: children
props.description: Item content and optional nested MenuList.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the item as the current one. It adds Bulma's `is-active` class, and `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, so assistive tech can tell which item is current too. An `aria-current` you pass wins, even `undefined`: use it to say something else (`"location"` for a section of one page, say), or `aria-current={false}` to turn it off. A menu should mark one page, so when the section above the current page is `active` too, give it `aria-current="location"`, and give an `active` item that isn't navigation, such as an `as="button"` filter, `aria-current={false}`.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the inner element `as` renders, not the wrapping `<li>`, typed from `as`: the DOM node for an intrinsic tag, or whatever handle a custom component exposes.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element or component selected by as (default <a>) and Bulma helper props
